strengths: UniDebugger addresses a relevant problem for language-model-based programming: integrating fault localization, contextual analysis, patch generation, and test feedback. The staged escalation provides a clear, practically motivated system design.

The reported Defects4J results are substantial: 197 correctly repaired bugs versus 157 for ChatRepair, including 42 fixes outside the compared baselines’ combined coverage. If validated, these constitute a useful empirical contribution.

Evaluation covers four benchmarks and three programming languages. UniDebugger-Lite improves plausible-fix counts across seven backbones on 600 ConDefects examples, providing evidence that its benefits extend beyond one model.

The manuscript supplies detailed agent prompts, execution examples, and a repository link. Distinguishing plausible from correct patches and replacing live web search with local retrieval during evaluation are useful methodological choices.
weaknesses: A concrete error undermines the worked correctness example. Appendix A.4 describes Figure 23 as successfully corrected, yet its boundary checks inspect the last significant hexadecimal digit through offsets +7/+15. For 0x80000000, this selects createInteger and reproduces the failure shown in Figure 16. This does not establish that aggregate results are wrong, but requires reconciliation with actual patch artifacts and test logs. The manual adjudication criteria behind the 197 correct fixes also need documentation.

The central benefit of hierarchical coordination is not isolated. Table 2 simultaneously increases agents, information, tool access, and computation. There is no budget-matched iterative single-agent baseline, always-L3 configuration, or alternative coordination control. These experiments demonstrate benefits from additional scaffolding without establishing which architectural choices cause them. Reporting only plausible fixes in the ablations also leaves their effect on semantic correctness unresolved.

The efficiency claim is inadequately supported. Five or twenty framework attempts are not directly comparable to baseline patch samples: each attempt can contain multiple agent calls, patch proposals, tests, and refinements. Table 2 reports expense per run without a comparable total-cost analysis against strong baselines. Same-backbone comparisons with matched budgets and cost per correctly repaired bug are needed to substantiate the claimed efficiency advantage.

The end-to-end localization assumption remains unclear. Every workflow receives a 'bug-located file'; the paper says unit testing identifies it but does not specify the selection procedure, ambiguity handling, or localization success rate. The evaluation should establish that this input is automatically obtained without benchmark annotations and explain how incorrect file selection affects the reported results.

Several numerical inconsistencies impede verification. The complete system produces 286 plausible Defects4J fixes in Table 1 but 291 in Tables 2 and 4 without an explained configuration difference. RewardRepair has 90 correct fixes but only 75 plausible fixes, contradicting the stated metric relationship. Codeflaws contains 3,902 bugs in the setup and 3,982 in the results. Corrected tables and traceable bug-level results are necessary.

Reproduction remains underspecified despite the supplied prompts. Exact model snapshots, decoding settings, the per-agent resampling limit m, and local retrieval configuration are not adequately documented. Algorithm 1 also returns unconditionally inside the outer attempt loop, preventing the stated repeated attempts as written. Together with the correctness and evaluation concerns, these are material revisions needed before a sound Findings recommendation.
